items.note: Author calls Udayaditya 'King Bhoj's successor' who added lustre to the Paramara kings' achievement (journalistic framing).
Reporter Govind Saxena's video of Udaipur was watched by more than a lakh of viewers; outside media interest.
Records a complaint that an archaeology department functionary saw in Udayaditya's city only Mughal and Mandu sultan encroachment, not what lay before.
A Hindi translation of a Persian farman of the period after Jahangir, headed 'Documents of the Jama Masjid and Mahal Qubba Udaipura', was presented in the tehsil to defend the palace occupation.
A Qazi family hung a private-property signboard in a corner of the ruined Paramara palace; it stayed for decades unchallenged by officials.
Within two weeks the encroachers were removed from the ruins of Udaipur's ancient palace; they handed the key to officers.

Per the farman as translated, in Jahangir's time Auliya Ibn Abdul Samad laid the foundation of the mosque and Mahal Qubba of Udaipur (Sarkar Chanderi, Suba Malwa); both half complete when the emperor died.

claim.value: Auliya Ibn Abdul Samad (Mahal Qubba and mosque, per Persian farman, Jahangir's time)

items.note: Farman text: Shah Jahan offered namaz in the mosque; worshippers to remember Firdaus-Makani and the emperor; dated 10 Zilhijja 1041 Hijri.
Author's reading: some four or five centuries after Udayaditya Udaipur remained but was a neglected town in the Chanderi suba, no longer in Paramara hands.
Chanderi Darwaza is a gate of Udaipur's fort wall, to the north, running parallel to the main road; gates were named after the city they faced.
Oldest inscription about the Paramara kings from Udaipur is of 1080; the second is of 1229, of Devapaladeva.
In Devapaladeva's time Iltutmish looted Vidisha and Ujjain and devastated Malwa; called the first Islamic contact of the region.
Paramara splendour ended at Mandu at the hands of a force sent by Alauddin Khilji; Mahlakdeva clashed with the Khiljis.
By 1528 Udaipur lay in the Chanderi Sarkar and entered a bad period under local occupiers appointed by the Mughals (author speculates on who they were).
Neelkantheshwar temple survived; pillars and doorframes of the palace precinct behind it testify to Paramara architecture.
Mosque pillars show Paramara work; the mosque stands in the palace's square precinct and was originally part of the palace, turned into a place of worship after Muslim occupation.
A signboard of illegal occupation hung in part of the palace for decades under many administrators.
Eviction order under Section 248 of the Indian Land Revenue Code prepared against a named Udaipur resident.
Order text: illegal occupation of 20x40 sq ft out of Khasra 822 (0.795 ha), village Udaipur; show-cause notice issued.
Order: evicted, fine of Rs 5000 under Section 248(1), occupation to be removed before 22.01.2021.
Remarks that the qaziyat of 84 villages was disposed of by the order.
Order sets liability of Rs 500 per day from 23.01.2021, civil-jail proceedings under Section 248(2A); dated 15 January 2021.
The Qazi had held the qaziyat of 84 villages, received in Mughal times, from the palace ruins; he handed over the keys of Udaipur Palace.
Vijay Mandir at Vidisha built by Paramara king Narvarman, Udayaditya's successor in the genealogy; author conjectures young Narvarman lived in Udaipur when the Neelkantheshwar temple was built.
Author judges the Vijay Mandir several times larger than Udaipur's temple, built to exceed Udayaditya's work.
Vidisha larger and more ancient than Udaipur; known history to the Mauryas, Sanchi stupas, Kalidasa's Meghaduta, Gupta period remains.
Vidisha's history reaches the Mauryas; stupas of Sanchi near Vidisha; Gupta-period proofs scattered in the region.
A Greek ambassador adopted the Vaishnava religion at Vidisha; recorded on a stone pillar by the Betwa, Khamba Baba, once a garuda-stambha; the Heliodorus inscription can still be read.
Vijay Mandir at Vidisha first razed in Iltutmish's attack; Minhaj Siraj gave the temple's height as 105 gaz.
Heliodorus changed his religion and had the declaration inscribed on a large pillar on the bank of the Vetravati (Betwa); literary retelling.
At Heliodorus's first coming the tales of Ashoka and Pushyamitra Shunga were fresh and the Sanchi stupas were under construction.
Literary device: Minhaj Siraj says the 105-gaz temple at Vidisha was destroyed by Iltutmish, who then set off toward Ujjain; first Islamic armies there.
Varaha image on the rock at Udayagiri; 1500-year-old Gupta inscription; Chandragupta and Dhruvaswamini episode.
Author says Udaipur has a deep relation with Raja Bhoj; Udayaditya became Maharaja only after him and must have prepared under his protection (author's inference).

claim.value: became Maharaja after Bhoj (author's inference of preparation under Bhoj)

items.note: The narrow six-to-seven-foot lane to the temple was widened by ten feet on each side; house and shop fronts removed (16 February 2021).
Ujjain was the first Paramara capital, which Bhoj shifted to Dhara; buildings of Bhoj's time were Sanskrit schools with Saraswati images.
Bhoj as scholar; a council of scholars of grammar, literature, music, water management, architecture, town planning, temple construction and vastu drew scholars from Kashmir.
Mahlakdeva called the last Paramara king; Iltutmish attacked Malwa in his time and temples were razed.
Dilawar Khan Ghori became the first independent sultan of Malwa.
Assessment of Bhoj: developed arts, honoured the virtuous, built, wrote books and founded knowledge-centres like the Saraswati-kanthabharana; remembered a thousand years later.
Lane cleared ten feet on each side; houses rebuilt; one house with the Jama Masjid signboard still jutted into the road.
Mallu Chand Jain's house beside the temple has broken temple remains inside and out; inner rooms ten centuries old, like a sanctum with carved stones.
House once buried in a mound; clearing found rooms built of splendidly carved stones.
Only three Jain families are left in Udaipur.
Shopkeeper Raja Miyan gave eight feet more space without waiting for a government order.
Author infers from a found instrument part that music was taught or musicians lived at the temple for the praises of Shiva (inference, not documented).
Paramara kings loved learning; experts in language, grammar, poetry, drama, vastu, architecture, astrology and music around them; Bhoj himself held the status of scholar.
Old stepwell near a brick-kiln with curving stone steps and an inscription.
Raja Mishra gave eight feet; 40 businessmen set back shops and houses; a 30-foot road had become a ten-foot lane.
Paramaras worshippers of Shiva; Udaipur one of the busiest commercial centres, with fort, palace, stepwells, gateways, temples, courthouse; layout visible on Google Map up the hill.
After the Paramaras, attacks by Iltutmish, Alauddin Khilji, Muhammad Tughlaq, Sher Shah; Babur's attack on Chanderi in 1528 and Udaipur became part of the Chanderi suba.
Author says artisans of mathematics, sculpture and painting must have come; places of worship were centres of education, culture and art.
An old residence with splendid artworks was excavated decades ago and cleaned; now a family's house.
Inscriptions of Udaipur were brought from the ASI archive, with English translations done long ago.
Author asks why a Hindi translation of the Sanskrit inscriptions is not displayed in the temple precinct to inform devotees and tourists.
News of the Udaipur efforts reached INTACH, a non-governmental organisation that looks after monuments.
INTACH's Bhopal convener offered to host the Udaipur PowerPoint presentation.
More than a hundred people attended the 'Katha Udaipur' presentation in Bhopal.
The presentation included three inscriptions as a timeline and a focus on water-bodies; stepwell photos recalled Rani-ki-Vav of Patan.
INTACH gave an introduction to the interest awakened toward Udaipur.
On the hill a rock-temple was begun by cutting the hill, like Ellora, but stopped at an initial stage; a few proofs exist.
Author suggests the hill rock-temple was meant to surpass Udayaditya's work, as Narvarman's Vijay Mandir at Vidisha tried to surpass his father's work in Udaipur (conjecture).
Author thinks the unfinished rock-temple is probably from the later Paramara period.
Vijay Mandir at Vidisha was ruined by Iltutmish a hundred years after Narvarman; a mosque was made from the rubble.
Author says the Sabha Mandal of old Bhopal was a temple precinct and Sanskrit school built after Bhoj, and that Udayaditya himself had it built.
Author says there is proof Bhopal was founded by Raja Bhoj; the Bada Talab spreads over 36 sq km on his dam.
Udaipur is a small town a morning's journey from Bhopal with return by evening.

claim.value: set out from Bhopal in the morning, return by evening

items.note: Author remarks on the inscriptions: as though the stones had been taken out of a printer; the craftsmen must have been skilful.
